media.ocr_text: A long-lived assistant that brings up memories without being asked must decide at every turn whether anything in its store is worth an interruption. We show that this decision is a multiple-testing problem whose difficulty grows with the store size N. On streaming replays of LongMemEval and LoCoMo, a similarity threshold tuned to 5% false alarms at N=8 reaches 87-100% at N=2048, across embedding models and for explicit and implicit cues; LLM judges show the same growth from a lower base. We prove that a gate with false-alarm rate α operates at a per-item false-positive rate of about -ln(1-α)/N, which pins its hit rate to the far left of the single-comparison ROC curve and, under regular variation, makes it decay as a power of N with an explicit constant. The resulting prediction matches the hit rate of a per-N oracle threshold to within one percentage point.
